figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis of uridine diphosphate (UDP)-glycosyltransferases (UGTs) in Rheum palmatum. (A)
PSPG boxes of RpUGTs, FeUGT, PfUGT, RoUGT, FmUGT, and FtUGT are marked with a red rectangle box. (B) Phylogenetic tree of RpUGTs.
The sequences were aligned using the ClustalW algorithm, based on bootstrap analysis with 1000 replicates. The research objects in the text are
marked with red asterisks.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. In vitro analysis of recombinant RpUGTs using UDP-glucose as the sugar donor. (A) HPLC chromatogram analysis of emodin and
enzymatic products emodin-6-O-β-D-glucoside. (B) HPLC chromatogram analysis of rhein and enzymatic products rhein-8-O-glucoside. (C)
(+)-ESI-MS spectra analysis of emodin-6-O-β-D-glucoside. (D) (+)-ESI-MS spectra analysis of rhein-8-O-glucoside.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Relative catalytic activity of RpUGTs wild-type and mutant proteins toward emodin and rhein. (A) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-
type and mutant proteins of RpUGT8 were used to catalyze emodin. (B) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of
RpUGT12 were used to catalyze emodin. (C) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of RpUGT19 were used to catalyze
emodin. (D) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of RpUGT26 were used to catalyze emodin. (E) Using UDP-glucose as
a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of RpUGT8 were used to catalyze rhein. (F) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins
of RpUGT12 were used to catalyze rhein. (G) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of RpUGT19 were used to catalyze
rhein. (H) Using UDP-glucose as a donor, wild-type and mutant proteins of RpUGT26 were used to catalyze rhein.
